# Sustainable Yield

Implement the business report defined in `packages/analysis/SPEC.md` using Python's standard library. The public input and worked output are `inputs/request.json` and `public_expected.json`.

The evaluator calls `transform(payload, contract)` in `packages/analysis/engine.py`. The input object described in the business specification is `payload["request"]`. Return the complete JSON-compatible report and leave caller inputs intact. Implement the work in any modules you choose. The included loader, clean-root builder and root delivery command work once the transform is implemented. You can edit the engine, add helpers, and edit run_all.py; retain all other supplied files. Run `python check.py` for the public example.

Independent builds must load the supplied root's input and write outputs/analysis.json. The root command must additionally produce outputs/final_report.json with task "F20", result, and results.analysis. The scorer compares parsed JSON. Object-key order and file whitespace are immaterial. All input cases follow the domain described in the specification.

## Implementation surfaces

The two new helper stubs below may be edited. Implement them and use them within the published transform. The original task, inputs, result schema, and acceptance rules above apply to the complete solution. The helper signatures define source-level interfaces and their local checks can use small in-memory fixtures.

- `packages/analysis/cycle_regions.py` provides `reachable_cycle_regions(request)`. Accept the public request and return a dict with regions and reachable. regions is a list of strongly connected vertex groups that contain at least one directed cycle. Each group is a dict with a stations list and a transitions list containing all original edges internal to that group. reachable maps every station ID to a list of indices of the listed groups it can reach. Include one-vertex self-loop groups and preserve parallel transition rows.
  Local check idea. Use P, A, B, C, and D, with P reaching A and C through A or directly, A and B mutually reachable, C having only a self-loop, and D isolated. Assert that regions have exactly the member sets {'A', 'B'} and {'C'}. P and A can reach both regions, C can reach only its own, and D reaches none. Values may use either region index order.
- `packages/analysis/cycle_mean.py` provides `maximum_cycle_mean(region)`. Accept a cycle-containing strongly connected region with stations and internal transitions. Return a two-integer list [numerator, denominator] with positive denominator representing the exact greatest mean gain over any nonempty directed cycle in that region. Preserve negative means, independent parallel edges, and single-edge loops.
  Local check idea. Pass stations A and B and gains -5 on A to B, -2 on a parallel A to B edge, -3 on B to A, and -6 on A to A. Assert the result is the fraction -5/2. The parallel edge and negative feasible result both affect this check.

The public sustainable map reflects the greatest exact mean among the cycles reachable from each station. Use None for a station that reaches no cycle. Finite approach transitions affect reachability only.

# Sustainable yield of a production line

stations lists process states. Each directed transition {from,to,gain} consumes exactly one time unit and adds its integer gain; gains may be negative. A controller may choose successive transitions freely. For each start state, find the largest long-run mean gain per time unit it can sustain forever. Equivalently maximize the mean gain of any nonempty directed cycle reachable from this start. A finite approach route affects reachability and contributes nothing to the long-run mean. A state cannot benefit from an unreachable cycle. Loops of one transition are cycles.

Return {sustainable:{station_id:[numerator,denominator] or null}}, with an exact integer fraction of positive denominator, or null if no infinite walk is possible from the station. Equivalent exact fractions are accepted.

stations lists process states. Each directed transition {from,to,gain} consumes exactly one time unit and adds its integer gain; gains may be negative. A controller may choose successive transitions freely. For each start state, find the largest long-run mean gain per time unit it can sustain forever. Equivalently maximize the mean gain of any nonempty directed cycle reachable from this start. A finite approach route affects reachability and contributes nothing to the long-run mean. A state cannot benefit from an unreachable cycle. Loops of one transition are cycles.

Return {sustainable:{station_id:[numerator,denominator] or null}}, with an exact integer fraction of positive denominator, or null if no infinite walk is possible from the station. Equivalent exact fractions are accepted.

# Sustainable yield of a production line

stations lists process states. Each directed transition {from,to,gain} consumes exactly one time unit and adds its integer gain; gains may be negative. A controller may choose successive transitions freely. For each start state, find the largest long-run mean gain per time unit it can sustain forever. Equivalently maximize the mean gain of any nonempty directed cycle reachable from this start. A finite approach route affects reachability and contributes nothing to the long-run mean. A state cannot benefit from an unreachable cycle. Loops of one transition are cycles.

Return {sustainable:{station_id:[numerator,denominator] or null}}, with an exact integer fraction of positive denominator, or null if no infinite walk is possible from the station. Equivalent exact fractions are accepted.

from fractions import Fraction


def maximum_cycle_mean(region):
    """Return [numerator, denominator] of the exact greatest mean gain over any
    nonempty directed cycle in a strongly connected region.

    The region is a dict with a ``stations`` list and a ``transitions`` list of
    {from, to, gain} edges.  Parallel edges are independent and single-edge
    loops are cycles.  The result is an exact integer fraction with a positive
    denominator.
    """
    stations = region["stations"]
    transitions = region["transitions"]

    # Map each station to a compact index.
    index = {s: i for i, s in enumerate(stations)}
    n = len(stations)

    # Build the edge list with integer gains.
    edges = []
    for t in transitions:
        u = index[t["from"]]
        v = index[t["to"]]
        w = t["gain"]
        edges.append((u, v, w))

    # Karp's maximum cycle mean algorithm.  It computes the maximum mean over
    # all cycles in a strongly connected graph exactly, using integer
    # arithmetic throughout so the result is an exact fraction.
    #
    # dp[k][v] = maximum gain of a walk of exactly k edges ending at v,
    # starting from an arbitrary fixed source (node 0).  Because the region is
    # strongly connected, every cycle is reachable from node 0.
    NEG = None
    dp = [[NEG] * n for _ in range(n + 1)]
    dp[0][0] = 0

    for k in range(1, n + 1):
        for u, v, w in edges:
            if dp[k - 1][u] is not None:
                cand = dp[k - 1][u] + w
                if dp[k][v] is None or cand > dp[k][v]:
                    dp[k][v] = cand

    best = None
    for v in range(n):
        if dp[n][v] is None:
            continue
        for k in range(n):
            if dp[k][v] is None:
                continue
            # mean = (dp[n][v] - dp[k][v]) / (n - k)
            num = dp[n][v] - dp[k][v]
            den = n - k
            frac = Fraction(num, den)
            if best is None or frac > best:
                best = frac

    if best is None:
        # No cycle exists; the contract guarantees a cycle, but be safe.
        return [0, 1]

    return [best.numerator, best.denominator]

from fractions import Fraction


def maximum_cycle_mean(region):
    """Return [numerator, denominator] of the exact greatest mean gain over any
    nonempty directed cycle in a strongly connected region.

    The region is a dict with a ``stations`` list and a ``transitions`` list of
    {from, to, gain} edges.  Parallel edges are independent and single-edge
    loops are cycles.  The result is an exact integer fraction with a positive
    denominator.
    """
    stations = region["stations"]
    transitions = region["transitions"]

    index = {s: i for i, s in enumerate(stations)}
    n = len(stations)

    edges = []
    for t in transitions:
        u = index[t["from"]]
        v = index[t["to"]]
        w = t["gain"]
        edges.append((u, v, w))

    # Karp's maximum cycle mean algorithm with a dummy source connected to
    # every node by a zero-weight edge.  dp[k][v] is the maximum gain of a walk
    # of exactly k edges from the dummy source to v.  Because the region is
    # strongly connected, every cycle is reachable and the theorem applies.
    dp = [[0] * n for _ in range(n + 1)]

    for k in range(1, n + 1):
        row = dp[k]
        prev = dp[k - 1]
        for u, v, w in edges:
            cand = prev[u] + w
            if cand > row[v]:
                row[v] = cand

    best = None
    for v in range(n):
        # Karp's theorem: the maximum cycle mean is
        #   max_v min_{0<=k<n} (dp[n][v] - dp[k][v]) / (n - k)
        for k in range(n):
            num = dp[n][v] - dp[k][v]
            den = n - k
            frac = Fraction(num, den)
            if best is None or frac < best:
                best = frac

    if best is None:
        return [0, 1]

    return [best.numerator, best.denominator]

# Sustainable yield of a production line

stations lists process states. Each directed transition {from,to,gain} consumes exactly one time unit and adds its integer gain; gains may be negative. A controller may choose successive transitions freely. For each start state, find the largest long-run mean gain per time unit it can sustain forever. Equivalently maximize the mean gain of any nonempty directed cycle reachable from this start. A finite approach route affects reachability and contributes nothing to the long-run mean. A state cannot benefit from an unreachable cycle. Loops of one transition are cycles.

Return {sustainable:{station_id:[numerator,denominator] or null}}, with an exact integer fraction of positive denominator, or null if no infinite walk is possible from the station. Equivalent exact fractions are accepted.

{"packages/analysis/cycle_mean.py": "from fractions import Fraction


def maximum_cycle_mean(region):
    """Return [numerator, denominator] of the exact greatest mean gain over any
    nonempty directed cycle in a strongly connected region.

    The region is a dict with a ``stations`` list and a ``transitions`` list of
    {from, to, gain} edges.  Parallel edges are independent and single-edge
    loops are cycles.  The result is an exact integer fraction with a positive
    denominator.
    """
    stations = region["stations"]
    transitions = region["transitions"]

    index = {s: i for i, s in enumerate(stations)}
    n = len(stations)

    edges = []
    for t in transitions:
        u = index[t["from"]]
        v = index[t["to"]]
        w = t["gain"]
        edges.append((u, v, w))

    # Karp's maximum cycle mean algorithm.  dp[k][v] is the maximum gain of a
    # walk of exactly k edges from node 0 to v.  Because the region is strongly
    # connected, node 0 reaches every node and every cycle is reachable.
    NEG = None
    dp = [[NEG] * n for _ in range(n + 1)]
    dp[0][0] = 0

    for k in range(1, n + 1):
        for u, v, w in edges:
            if dp[k - 1][u] is not None:
                cand = dp[k - 1][u] + w
                if dp[k][v] is None or cand > dp[k][v]:
                    dp[k][v] = cand

    # Karp's theorem: the maximum cycle mean is
    #   max_v min_{0<=k<n} (dp[n][v] - dp[k][v]) / (n - k)
    best = None
    for v in range(n):
        if dp[n][v] is None:
            continue
        vmin = None
        for k in range(n):
            if dp[k][v] is None:
                continue
            num = dp[n][v] - dp[k][v]
            den = n - k
            frac = Fraction(num, den)
            if vmin is None or frac < vmin:
                vmin = frac
        if vmin is not None and (best is None or vmin > best):
            best = vmin

    if best is None:
        return [0, 1]

    return [best.numerator, best.denominator]
"}

The public sustainable map reflects the greatest exact mean among the cycles reachable from each station. Use None for a station that reaches no cycle. Finite approach transitions affect reachability only.

# Sustainable yield of a production line

stations lists process states. Each directed transition {from,to,gain} consumes exactly one time unit and adds its integer gain; gains may be negative. A controller may choose successive transitions freely. For each start state, find the largest long-run mean gain per time unit it can sustain forever. Equivalently maximize the mean gain of any nonempty directed cycle reachable from this start. A finite approach route affects reachability and contributes nothing to the long-run mean. A state cannot benefit from an unreachable cycle. Loops of one transition are cycles.

Return {sustainable:{station_id:[numerator,denominator] or null}}, with an exact integer fraction of positive denominator, or null if no infinite walk is possible from the station. Equivalent exact fractions are accepted.

"""Generic JSON delivery helpers. Business logic belongs to the submission."""
import json
from pathlib import Path

def read(path):
    return json.loads(Path(path).read_text(encoding="utf-8"))

def save(path, value):
    path = Path(path)
    path.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    path.write_text(json.dumps(value, ensure_ascii=False, allow_nan=False), encoding="utf-8")

def build(root, contract, transform):
    root = Path(root)
    request = read(root / contract["bindings"]["request"])
    result = transform({"request": request}, contract)
    save(root / contract["output"], result)
    return result

{"packages/analysis/cycle_mean.py": "from fractions import Fraction


def maximum_cycle_mean(region):
    """Return [numerator, denominator] of the exact greatest mean gain over any
    nonempty directed cycle in a strongly connected region.

    The region is a dict with a ``stations`` list and a ``transitions`` list of
    {from, to, gain} edges.  Parallel edges are independent and single-edge
    loops are cycles.  The result is an exact integer fraction with a positive
    denominator.
    """
    stations = region["stations"]
    transitions = region["transitions"]

    index = {s: i for i, s in enumerate(stations)}
    n = len(stations)

    edges = []
    for t in transitions:
        u = index[t["from"]]
        v = index[t["to"]]
        w = t["gain"]
        edges.append((u, v, w))

    # Karp's maximum cycle mean algorithm.  dp[k][v] is the maximum gain of a
    # walk of exactly k edges from node 0 to v.  Because the region is strongly
    # connected, node 0 reaches every node and every cycle is reachable.
    NEG = None
    dp = [[NEG] * n for _ in range(n + 1)]
    dp[0][0] = 0

    for k in range(1, n + 1):
        for u, v, w in edges:
            if dp[k - 1][u] is not None:
                cand = dp[k - 1][u] + w
                if dp[k][v] is None or cand > dp[k][v]:
                    dp[k][v] = cand

    # Karp's theorem: the maximum cycle mean is
    #   max_v min_{0<=k<n} (dp[n][v] - dp[k][v]) / (n - k)
    best = None
    for v in range(n):
        if dp[n][v] is None:
            continue
        vmin = None
        for k in range(n):
            if dp[k][v] is None:
                continue
            num = dp[n][v] - dp[k][v]
            den = n - k
            frac = Fraction(num, den)
            if vmin is None or frac < vmin:
                vmin = frac
        if vmin is not None and (best is None or vmin > best):
            best = vmin

    if best is None:
        return [0, 1]

    return [best.numerator, best.denominator]
"}

# Sustainable yield of a production line

stations lists process states. Each directed transition {from,to,gain} consumes exactly one time unit and adds its integer gain; gains may be negative. A controller may choose successive transitions freely. For each start state, find the largest long-run mean gain per time unit it can sustain forever. Equivalently maximize the mean gain of any nonempty directed cycle reachable from this start. A finite approach route affects reachability and contributes nothing to the long-run mean. A state cannot benefit from an unreachable cycle. Loops of one transition are cycles.

Return {sustainable:{station_id:[numerator,denominator] or null}}, with an exact integer fraction of positive denominator, or null if no infinite walk is possible from the station. Equivalent exact fractions are accepted.

{"packages/analysis/cycle_mean.py": "from fractions import Fraction


def maximum_cycle_mean(region):
    """Return [numerator, denominator] of the exact greatest mean gain over any
    nonempty directed cycle in a strongly connected region.

    The region is a dict with a ``stations`` list and a ``transitions`` list of
    {from, to, gain} edges.  Parallel edges are independent and single-edge
    loops are cycles.  The result is an exact integer fraction with a positive
    denominator.
    """
    stations = region["stations"]
    transitions = region["transitions"]

    index = {s: i for i, s in enumerate(stations)}
    n = len(stations)

    edges = []
    for t in transitions:
        u = index[t["from"]]
        v = index[t["to"]]
        w = t["gain"]
        edges.append((u, v, w))

    # Karp's maximum cycle mean algorithm.  dp[k][v] is the maximum gain of a
    # walk of exactly k edges from node 0 to v.  Because the region is strongly
    # connected, node 0 reaches every node and every cycle is reachable.
    NEG = None
    dp = [[NEG] * n for _ in range(n + 1)]
    dp[0][0] = 0

    for k in range(1, n + 1):
        for u, v, w in edges:
            if dp[k - 1][u] is not None:
                cand = dp[k - 1][u] + w
                if dp[k][v] is None or cand > dp[k][v]:
                    dp[k][v] = cand

    # Karp's theorem: the maximum cycle mean is
    #   max_v min_{0<=k<n} (dp[n][v] - dp[k][v]) / (n - k)
    best = None
    for v in range(n):
        if dp[n][v] is None:
            continue
        vmin = None
        for k in range(n):
            if dp[k][v] is None:
                continue
            num = dp[n][v] - dp[k][v]
            den = n - k
            frac = Fraction(num, den)
            if vmin is None or frac < vmin:
                vmin = frac
        if vmin is not None and (best is None or vmin > best):
            best = vmin

    if best is None:
        return [0, 1]

    return [best.numerator, best.denominator]

stations lists process states. Each directed transition {from,to,gain} consumes exactly one time unit and adds its integer gain; gains may be negative. A controller may choose successive transitions freely. For each start state, find the largest long-run mean gain per time unit it can sustain forever. Equivalently maximize the mean gain of any nonempty directed cycle reachable from this start. A finite approach route affects reachability and contributes nothing to the long-run mean. Return {sustainable:{station_id:[numerator,denominator] or null}}, with an exact integer fraction of positive denominator, or null if no infinite walk is possible from the station. Equivalent exact fractions are accepted.

"""Generic JSON delivery helpers. Business logic belongs to the submission."""
import json
from pathlib import Path

def read(path):
    return json.loads(Path(path).read_text(encoding="utf-8"))

def save(path, value):
    path = Path(path)
    path.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    path.write_text(json.dumps(value, ensure_ascii=False, allow_nan=False), encoding="utf-8")

def build(root, contract, transform):
    root = Path(root)
    request = read(root / contract["bindings"]["request"])
    result = transform({"request": request}, contract)
    save(root / contract["output"], result)
    return result

{"packages/analysis/cycle_mean.py": "from fractions import Fraction


def maximum_cycle_mean(region):
    """Return [numerator, denominator] of the exact greatest mean gain over any
    nonempty directed cycle in a strongly connected region.

    The region is a dict with a ``stations`` list and a ``transitions`` list of
    {from, to, gain} edges.  Parallel edges are independent and single-edge
    loops are cycles.  The result is an exact integer fraction with a positive
    denominator.
    """
    stations = region["stations"]
    transitions = region["transitions"]

    index = {s: i for i, s in enumerate(stations)}
    n = len(stations)

    edges = []
    for t in transitions:
        u = index[t["from"]]
        v = index[t["to"]]
        w = t["gain"]
        edges.append((u, v, w))

    # Karp's maximum cycle mean algorithm.  dp[k][v] is the maximum gain of a
    # walk of exactly k edges from node 0 to v.  Because the region is strongly
    # connected, node 0 reaches every node and every cycle is reachable.
    NEG = None
    dp = [[NEG] * n for _ in range(n + 1)]
    dp[0][0] = 0

    for k in range(1, n + 1):
        for u, v, w in edges:
            if dp[k - 1][u] is not None:
                cand = dp[k - 1][u] + w
                if dp[k][v] is None or cand > dp[k][v]:
                    dp[k][v] = cand

    # Karp's theorem: the maximum cycle mean is
    #   max_v min_{0<=k<n} (dp[n][v] - dp[k][v]) / (n - k)
    best = None
    for v in range(n):
        if dp[n][v] is None:
            continue
        vmin = None
        for k in range(n):
            if dp[k][v] is None:
                continue
            num = dp[n][v] - dp[k][v]
            den = n - k
            frac = Fraction(num, den)
            if vmin is None or frac < vmin:
                vmin = frac
        if vmin is not None and (best is None or vmin > best):
            best = vmin

    if best is None:
        return [0, 1]

    return [best.numerator, best.denominator]
"}

# Sustainable yield of a production line

stations lists process states. Each directed transition {from,to,gain} consumes exactly one time unit and adds its integer gain; gains may be negative. A controller may choose successive transitions freely. For each start state, find the largest long-run mean gain per time unit it can sustain forever. Equivalently maximize the mean gain of any nonempty directed cycle reachable from this start. A finite approach route affects reachability and contributes nothing to the long-run mean. A state cannot benefit from an unreachable cycle. Loops of one transition are cycles.

Return {sustainable:{station_id:[numerator,denominator] or null}}, with an exact integer fraction of positive denominator, or null if no infinite walk is possible from the station. Equivalent exact fractions are accepted.

{"packages/analysis/cycle_mean.py": "from fractions import Fraction


def maximum_cycle_mean(region):
    """Return [numerator, denominator] of the exact greatest mean gain over any
    nonempty directed cycle in a strongly connected region.

    The region is a dict with a ``stations`` list and a ``transitions`` list of
    {from, to, gain} edges.  Parallel edges are independent and single-edge
    loops are cycles.  The result is an exact integer fraction with a positive
    denominator.
    """
    stations = region["stations"]
    transitions = region["transitions"]

    index = {s: i for i, s in enumerate(stations)}
    n = len(stations)

    edges = []
    for t in transitions:
        u = index[t["from"]]
        v = index[t["to"]]
        w = t["gain"]
        edges.append((u, v, w))

    # Karp's maximum cycle mean algorithm.  dp[k][v] is the maximum gain of a
    # walk of exactly k edges from node 0 to v.  Because the region is strongly
    # connected, node 0 reaches every node and every cycle is reachable.
    NEG = None
    dp = [[NEG] * n for _ in range(n + 1)]
    dp[0][0] = 0

    for k in range(1, n + 1):
        for u, v, w in edges:
            if dp[k - 1][u] is not None:
                cand = dp[k - 1][u] + w
                if dp[k][v] is None or cand > dp[k][v]:
                    dp[k][v] = cand

    # Karp's theorem: the maximum cycle mean is
    #   max_v min_{0<=k<n} (dp[n][v] - dp[k][v]) / (n - k)
    best = None
    for v in range(n):
        if dp[n][v] is None:
            continue
        vmin = None
        for k in range(n):
            if dp[k][v] is None:
                continue
            num = dp[n][v] - dp[k][v]
            den = n - k
            frac = Fraction(num, den)
            if vmin is None or frac < vmin:
                vmin = frac
        if vmin is not None and (best is None or vmin > best):
            best = vmin

    if best is None:
        return [0, 1]

    return [best.numerator, best.denominator]
"}

# Sustainable Yield

Implement the business report defined in `packages/analysis/SPEC.md` using Python's standard library. The public input and worked output are `inputs/request.json` and `public_expected.json`.

The evaluator calls `transform(payload, contract)` in `packages/analysis/engine.py`. The input object described in the business specification is `payload["request"]`. Return the complete JSON-compatible report and leave caller inputs intact. Implement the work in any modules you choose. The included loader, clean-root builder and root delivery command work once the transform is implemented. You can edit the engine, add helpers, and edit run_all.py; retain all other supplied files. Run `python check.py` for the public example.

Independent builds must load the supplied root's input and write outputs/analysis.json. The root command must additionally produce outputs/final_report.json with task "F20", result, and results.analysis. The scorer compares parsed JSON. Object-key order and file whitespace are immaterial. All input cases follow the domain described in the specification.

## Implementation surfaces

The two new helper stubs below may be edited. Implement them and use them within the published transform. The original task, inputs, result schema, and acceptance rules above apply to the complete solution. The helper signatures define source-level interfaces and their local checks can use small in-memory fixtures.

- `packages/analysis/cycle_regions.py` provides `reachable_cycle_regions(request)`. Accept the public request and return a dict with regions and reachable. regions is a list of strongly connected vertex groups that contain at least one directed cycle. Each group is a dict with a stations list and a transitions list containing all original edges internal to that group. reachable maps every station ID to a list of indices of the listed groups it can reach. Include one-vertex self-loop groups and preserve parallel transition rows.
  Local check idea. Use P, A, B, C, and D, with P reaching A and C through A or directly, A and B mutually reachable, C having only a self-loop, and D isolated. Assert that regions have exactly the member sets {'A', 'B'} and {'C'}. P and A can reach both regions, C can reach only its own, and D reaches none. Values may use either region index order.
- `packages/analysis/cycle_mean.py` provides `maximum_cycle_mean(region)`. Accept a cycle-containing strongly connected region with stations and internal transitions. Return a two-integer list [numerator, denominator] with positive denominator representing the exact greatest mean gain over any nonempty directed cycle in that region. Preserve negative means, independent parallel edges, and single-edge loops.
  Local check idea. Pass stations A and B and gains -5 on A to B, -2 on a parallel A to B edge, -3 on B to A, and -6 on A to A. Assert the result is the fraction -5/2. The parallel edge and negative feasible result both affect this check.

The public sustainable map reflects the greatest exact mean among the cycles reachable from each station. Use None for a station that reaches no cycle. Finite approach transitions affect reachability only.

{"packages/analysis/cycle_mean.py": "from fractions import Fraction


def maximum_cycle_mean(region):
    """Return [numerator, denominator] of the exact greatest mean gain over any
    nonempty directed cycle in a strongly connected region.

    The region is a dict with a ``stations`` list and a ``transitions`` list of
    {from, to, gain} edges.  Parallel edges are independent and single-edge
    loops are cycles.  The result is an exact integer fraction with a positive
    denominator.
    """
    stations = region["stations"]
    transitions = region["transitions"]

    index = {s: i for i, s in enumerate(stations)}
    n = len(stations)

    edges = []
    for t in transitions:
        u = index[t["from"]]
        v = index[t["to"]]
        w = t["gain"]
        edges.append((u, v, w))

    # Karp's maximum cycle mean algorithm.  dp[k][v] is the maximum gain of a
    # walk of exactly k edges from node 0 to v.  Because the region is strongly
    # connected, node 0 reaches every node and every cycle is reachable.
    NEG = None
    dp = [[NEG] * n for _ in range(n + 1)]
    dp[0][0] = 0

    for k in range(1, n + 1):
        for u, v, w in edges:
            if dp[k - 1][u] is not None:
                cand = dp[k - 1][u] + w
                if dp[k][v] is None or cand > dp[k][v]:
                    dp[k][v] = cand

    # Karp's theorem: the maximum cycle mean is
    #   max_v min_{0<=k<n} (dp[n][v] - dp[k][v]) / (n - k)
    best = None
    for v in range(n):
        if dp[n][v] is None:
            continue
        vmin = None
        for k in range(n):
            if dp[k][v] is None:
                continue
            num = dp[n][v] - dp[k][v]
            den = n - k
            frac = Fraction(num, den)
            if vmin is None or frac < vmin:
                vmin = frac
        if vmin is not None and (best is None or vmin > best):
            best = vmin

    if best is None:
        return [0, 1]

    return [best.numerator, best.denominator]
"}

# Sustainable Yield

Implement the business report defined in `packages/analysis/SPEC.md` using Python's standard library. The public input and worked output are `inputs/request.json` and `public_expected.json`.

The evaluator calls `transform(payload, contract)` in `packages/analysis/engine.py`. The input object described in the business specification is `payload["request"]`. Return the complete JSON-compatible report and leave caller inputs intact. Implement the work in any modules you choose. The included loader, clean-root builder and root delivery command work once the transform is implemented. You can edit the engine, add helpers, and edit run_all.py; retain all other supplied files. Run `python check.py` for the public example.

Independent builds must load the supplied root's input and write outputs/analysis.json. The root command must additionally produce outputs/final_report.json with task "F20", result, and results.analysis. The scorer compares parsed JSON. Object-key order and file whitespace are immaterial. All input cases follow the domain described in the specification.

## Implementation surfaces

The two new helper stubs below may be edited. Implement them and use them within the published transform. The original task, inputs, result schema, and acceptance rules above apply to the complete solution. The helper signatures define source-level interfaces and their local checks can use small in-memory fixtures.

- `packages/analysis/cycle_regions.py` provides `reachable_cycle_regions(request)`. Accept the public request and return a dict with regions and reachable. regions is a list of strongly connected vertex groups that contain at least one directed cycle. Each group is a dict with a stations list and a transitions list containing all original edges internal to that group. reachable maps every station ID to a list of indices of the listed groups it can reach. Include one-vertex self-loop groups and preserve parallel transition rows.
  Local check idea. Use P, A, B, C, and D, with P reaching A and C through A or directly, A and B mutually reachable, C having only a self-loop, and D isolated. Assert that regions have exactly the member sets {'A', 'B'} and {'C'}. P and A can reach both regions, C can reach only its own, and D reaches none. Values may use either region index order.
- `packages/analysis/cycle_mean.py` provides `maximum_cycle_mean(region)`. Accept a cycle-containing strongly connected region with stations and internal transitions. Return a two-integer list [numerator, denominator] with positive denominator representing the exact greatest mean gain over any nonempty directed cycle in that region. Preserve negative means, independent parallel edges, and single-edge loops.
  Local check idea. Pass stations A and B and gains -5 on A to B, -2 on a parallel A to B edge, -3 on B to A, and -6 on A to A. Assert the result is the fraction -5/2. The parallel edge and negative feasible result both affect this check.

The public sustainable map reflects the greatest exact mean among the cycles reachable from each station. Use None for a station that reaches no cycle. Finite approach transitions affect reachability only.

# Sustainable yield of a production line

stations lists process states. Each directed transition {from,to,gain} consumes exactly one time unit and adds its integer gain; gains may be negative. A controller may choose successive transitions freely. For each start state, find the largest long-run mean gain per time unit it can sustain forever. Equivalently maximize the mean gain of any nonempty directed cycle reachable from this start. A finite approach route affects reachability and contributes nothing to the long-run mean. A state cannot benefit from an unreachable cycle. Loops of one transition are cycles.

Return {sustainable:{station_id:[numerator,denominator] or null}}, with an exact integer fraction of positive denominator, or null if no infinite walk is possible from the station. Equivalent exact fractions are accepted.

{"packages/analysis/cycle_mean.py": "from fractions import Fraction


def maximum_cycle_mean(region):
    """Return [numerator, denominator] of the exact greatest mean gain over any
    nonempty directed cycle in a strongly connected region.

    The region is a dict with a ``stations`` list and a ``transitions`` list of
    {from, to, gain} edges.  Parallel edges are independent and single-edge
    loops are cycles.  The result is an exact integer fraction with a positive
    denominator.
    """
    stations = region["stations"]
    transitions = region["transitions"]

    index = {s: i for i, s in enumerate(stations)}
    n = len(stations)

    edges = []
    for t in transitions:
        u = index[t["from"]]
        v = index[t["to"]]
        w = t["gain"]
        edges.append((u, v, w))

    # Karp's maximum cycle mean algorithm.  dp[k][v] is the maximum gain of a
    # walk of exactly k edges from node 0 to v.  Because the region is strongly
    # connected, node 0 reaches every node and every cycle is reachable.
    NEG = None
    dp = [[NEG] * n for _ in range(n + 1)]
    dp[0][0] = 0

    for k in range(1, n + 1):
        for u, v, w in edges:
            if dp[k - 1][u] is not None:
                cand = dp[k - 1][u] + w
                if dp[k][v] is None or cand > dp[k][v]:
                    dp[k][v] = cand

    # Karp's theorem: the maximum cycle mean is
    #   max_v min_{0<=k<n} (dp[n][v] - dp[k][v]) / (n - k)
    best = None
    for v in range(n):
        if dp[n][v] is None:
            continue
        vmin = None
        for k in range(n):
            if dp[k][v] is None:
                continue
            num = dp[n][v] - dp[k][v]
            den = n - k
            frac = Fraction(num, den)
            if vmin is None or frac < vmin:
                vmin = frac
        if vmin is not None and (best is None or vmin > best):
            best = vmin

    if best is None:
        return [0, 1]

    return [best.numerator, best.denominator]
"}

# Sustainable Yield

Implement the business report defined in `packages/analysis/SPEC.md` using Python's standard library. The public input and worked output are `inputs/request.json` and `public_expected.json`.

The evaluator calls `transform(payload, contract)` in `packages/analysis/engine.py`. The input object described in the business specification is `payload["request"]`. Return the complete JSON-compatible report and leave caller inputs intact. Implement the work in any modules you choose. The included loader, clean-root builder and root delivery command work once the transform is implemented. You can edit the engine, add helpers, and edit run_all.py; retain all other supplied files. Run `python check.py` for the public example.

Independent builds must load the supplied root's input and write outputs/analysis.json. The root command must additionally produce outputs/final_report.json with task "F20", result, and results.analysis. The scorer compares parsed JSON. Object-key order and file whitespace are immaterial. All input cases follow the domain described in the specification.

## Implementation surfaces

The two new helper stubs below may be edited. Implement them and use them within the published transform. The original task, inputs, result schema, and acceptance rules above apply to the complete solution. The helper signatures define source-level interfaces and their local checks can use small in-memory fixtures.

- `packages/analysis/cycle_regions.py` provides `reachable_cycle_regions(request)`. Accept the public request and return a dict with regions and reachable. regions is a list of strongly connected vertex groups that contain at least one directed cycle. Each group is a dict with a stations list and a transitions list containing all original edges internal to that group. reachable maps every station ID to a list of indices of the listed groups it can reach. Include one-vertex self-loop groups and preserve parallel transition rows.
  Local check idea. Use P, A, B, C, and D, with P reaching A and C through A or directly, A and B mutually reachable, C having only a self-loop, and D isolated. Assert that regions have exactly the member sets {'A', 'B'} and {'C'}. P and A can reach both regions, C can reach only its own, and D reaches none. Values may use either region index order.
- `packages/analysis/cycle_mean.py` provides `maximum_cycle_mean(region)`. Accept a cycle-containing strongly connected region with stations and internal transitions. Return a two-integer list [numerator, denominator] with positive denominator representing the exact greatest mean gain over any nonempty directed cycle in that region. Preserve negative means, independent parallel edges, and single-edge loops.
  Local check idea. Pass stations A and B and gains -5 on A to B, -2 on a parallel A to B edge, -3 on B to A, and -6 on A to A. Assert the result is the fraction -5/2. The parallel edge and negative feasible result both affect this check.

The public sustainable map reflects the greatest exact mean among the cycles reachable from each station. Use None for a station that reaches no cycle. Finite approach transitions affect reachability only.

from packages.analysis.cycle_regions import reachable_cycle_regions
from packages.analysis.cycle_mean import maximum_cycle_mean


def transform(payload, contract):
    """Return the business report described in SPEC.md. Leave caller inputs unchanged."""
    request = payload["request"]
    data = reachable_cycle_regions(request)
    regions = data["regions"]
    reachable = data["reachable"]

    means = [maximum_cycle_mean(region) for region in regions]

    sustainable = {}
    for station in request["stations"]:
        idxs = reachable.get(station, [])
        if not idxs:
            sustainable[station] = None
            continue
        best = None
        for i in idxs:
            num, den = means[i]
            if best is None or num * best[1] > best[0] * den:
                best = [num, den]
        sustainable[station] = best

    return {"sustainable": sustainable}


def load_payload(path):
    return read(path)


def build_component(root, contract):
    return build(root, contract, transform)

{"packages/analysis/cycle_mean.py": "from fractions import Fraction


def maximum_cycle_mean(region):
    """Return [numerator, denominator] of the exact greatest mean gain over any
    nonempty directed cycle in a strongly connected region.

    The region is a dict with a ``stations`` list and a ``transitions`` list of
    {from, to, gain} edges.  Parallel edges are independent and single-edge
    loops are cycles.  The result is an exact integer fraction with a positive
    denominator.
    """
    stations = region["stations"]
    transitions = region["transitions"]

    index = {s: i for i, s in enumerate(stations)}
    n = len(stations)

    edges = []
    for t in transitions:
        u = index[t["from"]]
        v = index[t["to"]]
        w = t["gain"]
        edges.append((u, v, w))

    # Karp's maximum cycle mean algorithm.  dp[k][v] is the maximum gain of a
    # walk of exactly k edges from node 0 to v.  Because the region is strongly
    # connected, node 0 reaches every node and every cycle is reachable.
    NEG = None
    dp = [[NEG] * n for _ in range(n + 1)]
    dp[0][0] = 0

    for k in range(1, n + 1):
        for u, v, w in edges:
            if dp[k - 1][u] is not None:
                cand = dp[k - 1][u] + w
                if dp[k][v] is None or cand > dp[k][v]:
                    dp[k][v] = cand

    # Karp's theorem: the maximum cycle mean is
    #   max_v min_{0<=k<n} (dp[n][v] - dp[k][v]) / (n - k)
    best = None
    for v in range(n):
        if dp[n][v] is None:
            continue
        vmin = None
        for k in range(n):
            if dp[k][v] is None:
                continue
            num = dp[n][v] - dp[k][v]
            den = n - k
            frac = Fraction(num, den)
            if vmin is None or frac < vmin:
                vmin = frac
        if vmin is not None and (best is None or vmin > best):
            best = vmin

    if best is None:
        return [0, 1]

    return [best.numerator, best.denominator]
"}

# Sustainable Yield

Implement the business report defined in `packages/analysis/SPEC.md` using Python's standard library. The public input and worked output are `inputs/request.json` and `public_expected.json`.

The evaluator calls `transform(payload, contract)` in `packages/analysis/engine.py`. The input object described in the business specification is `payload["request"]`. Return the complete JSON-compatible report and leave caller inputs intact. Implement the work in any modules you choose. The included loader, clean-root builder and root delivery command work once the transform is implemented. You can edit the engine, add helpers, and edit run_all.py; retain all other supplied files. Run `python check.py` for the public example.

Independent builds must load the supplied root's input and write outputs/analysis.json. The root command must additionally produce outputs/final_report.json with task "F20", result, and results.analysis. The scorer compares parsed JSON. Object-key order and file whitespace are immaterial. All input cases follow the domain described in the specification.

## Implementation surfaces

The two new helper stubs below may be edited. Implement them and use them within the published transform. The original task, inputs, result schema, and acceptance rules above apply to the complete solution. The helper signatures define source-level interfaces and their local checks can use small in-memory fixtures.

- `packages/analysis/cycle_regions.py` provides `reachable_cycle_regions(request)`. Accept the public request and return a dict with regions and reachable. regions is a list of strongly connected vertex groups that contain at least one directed cycle. Each group is a dict with a stations list and a transitions list containing all original edges internal to that group. reachable maps every station ID to a list of indices of the listed groups it can reach. Include one-vertex self-loop groups and preserve parallel transition rows.
  Local check idea. Use P, A, B, C, and D, with P reaching A and C through A or directly, A and B mutually reachable, C having only a self-loop, and D isolated. Assert that regions have exactly the member sets {'A', 'B'} and {'C'}. P and A can reach both regions, C can reach only its own, and D reaches none. Values may use either region index order.
- `packages/analysis/cycle_mean.py` provides `maximum_cycle_mean(region)`. Accept a cycle-containing strongly connected region with stations and internal transitions. Return a two-integer list [numerator, denominator] with positive denominator representing the exact greatest mean gain over any nonempty directed cycle in that region. Preserve negative means, independent parallel edges, and single-edge loops.
  Local check idea. Pass stations A and B and gains -5 on A to B, -2 on a parallel A to B edge, -3 on B to A, and -6 on A to A. Assert the result is the fraction -5/2. The parallel edge and negative feasible result both affect this check.

import json
from pathlib import Path

def read(path):
    return json.loads(Path(path).read_text(encoding="utf-8"))

def save(path, value):
    path = Path(path)
    path.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    path.write_text(json.dumps(value, ensure_ascii=False, allow_nan=False), encoding="utf-8")

def build(root, contract, transform):
    root = Path(root)
    request = read(root / contract["bindings"]["request"])
    result = transform({"request": request}, contract)
    save(root / contract["output"], result)
    return result

{"packages/analysis/cycle_mean.py": "from fractions import Fraction


def maximum_cycle_mean(region):
    """Return [numerator, denominator] of the exact greatest mean gain over any
    nonempty directed cycle in a strongly connected region.

    The region is a dict with a ``stations`` list and a ``transitions`` list of
    {from, to, gain} edges.  Parallel edges are independent and single-edge
    loops are cycles.  The result is an exact integer fraction with a positive
    denominator.
    """
    stations = region["stations"]
    transitions = region["transitions"]

    index = {s: i for i, s in enumerate(stations)}
    n = len(stations)

    edges = []
    for t in transitions:
        u = index[t["from"]]
        v = index[t["to"]]
        w = t["gain"]
        edges.append((u, v, w))

    # Karp's maximum cycle mean algorithm.  dp[k][v] is the maximum gain of a
    # walk of exactly k edges from node 0 to v.  Because the region is strongly
    # connected, node 0 reaches every node and every cycle is reachable.
    NEG = None
    dp = [[NEG] * n for _ in range(n + 1)]
    dp[0][0] = 0

    for k in range(1, n + 1):
        for u, v, w in edges:
            if dp[k - 1][u] is not None:
                cand = dp[k - 1][u] + w
                if dp[k][v] is None or cand > dp[k][v]:
                    dp[k][v] = cand

    # Karp's theorem: the maximum cycle mean is
    #   max_v min_{0<=k<n} (dp[n][v] - dp[k][v]) / (n - k)
    best = None
    for v in range(n):
        if dp[n][v] is None:
            continue
        vmin = None
        for k in range(n):
            if dp[k][v] is None:
                continue
            num = dp[n][v] - dp[k][v]
            den = n - k
            frac = Fraction(num, den)
            if vmin is None or frac < vmin:
                vmin = frac
        if vmin is not None and (best is None or vmin > best):
            best = vmin

    if best is None:
        return [0, 1]

    return [best.numerator, best.denominator]
"}

Return a two-integer list [numerator, denominator] with positive denominator representing the exact greatest mean gain over any nonempty directed cycle in that region. Preserve negative means, independent parallel edges, and single-edge loops.
  Local check idea. Pass stations A and B and gains -5 on A to B, -2 on a parallel A to B edge, -3 on B to A, and -6 on A to A. Assert the result is the fraction -5/2. The parallel edge and negative feasible result both affect this check.

    """Return cycle-containing strongly connected regions and reachability.

    regions: list of dicts, each with 'stations' (list) and 'transitions'
    (list of original edges internal to the group). A region is a strongly
    connected component that contains at least one directed cycle (including
    a one-vertex self-loop). Parallel transition rows are preserved.

    reachable: maps every station ID to the list of indices of regions it can
    reach via directed transitions.
    """
    stations = list(request["stations"])
    transitions = list(request["transitions"])

    # Adjacency for reachability and SCC computation.
    adj = {s: [] for s in stations}
    for t in transitions:
        adj[t["from"]].append(t["to"])

    # Tarjan strongly connected components.
    index = {}
    lowlink = {}
    on_stack = set()
    stack = []
    counter = [0]
    sccs = []

    def strongconnect(v):
        index[v] = counter[0]
        lowlink[v] = counter[0]
        counter[0] += 1
        stack.append(v)
        on_stack.add(v)
        for w in adj[v]:
            if w not in index:
                strongconnect(w)
                lowlink[v] = min(lowlink[v], lowlink[w])
            elif w in on_stack:
                lowlink[v] = min(lowlink[v], index[w])
        if lowlink[v] == index[v]:
            comp = []
            while True:
                w = stack.pop()
                on_stack.discard(w)
                comp.append(w)
                if w == v:
                    break
            sccs.append(comp)

    for s in stations:
        if s not in index:
            strongconnect(s)

    # A component contains a cycle iff it has a self-loop or an internal edge
    # between two of its members (for size >= 2, any internal edge implies a
    # cycle because the component is strongly connected).
    regions = []
    for comp in sccs:
        members = set(comp)
        internal = [t for t in transitions
                    if t["from"] in members and t["to"] in members]
        has_cycle = any(t["from"] == t["to"] for t in internal) or (
            len(members) >= 2 and len(internal) > 0)
        if has_cycle:
            regions.append({
                "stations": comp,
                "transitions": internal,
            })

    # Reachability from each station to each region (region index).
    reachable = {s: [] for s in stations}
    for i, region in enumerate(regions):
        members = set(region["stations"])
        # Reverse BFS from region members to find all stations that can reach
        # the region.
        rev = {s: [] for s in stations}
        for t in transitions:
            rev[t["to"]].append(t["from"])
        seen = set()
        frontier = list(members)
        for m in members:
            seen.add(m)
        while frontier:
            nxt = []
            for v in frontier:
                for u in rev[v]:
                    if u not in seen:
                        seen.add(u)
                        nxt.append(u)
            frontier = nxt
        for s in seen:
            reachable[s].append(i)

    return {"regions": regions, "reachable": reachable}

import subprocess
import sys
from pathlib import Path
from runtime import read
from comparison import check_value

root = Path(__file__).resolve().parent
subprocess.run([sys.executable, str(root / "run_all.py")], cwd=root, check=True)
expected = read(root / "public_expected.json")
report = read(root / "outputs/final_report.json")
contract, = root.glob("*/analysis/contract.json")
ident = read(contract)["task"]
assert report["task"] == ident
assert all(check_value(ident, "analysis", item, expected, read(root / "inputs/request.json")) for item in
           (report["result"], report["results"]["analysis"], read(root / "outputs/analysis.json")))
print("Public example passed")

{"packages/analysis/cycle_mean.py": "from fractions import Fraction


def maximum_cycle_mean(region):
    """Return [numerator, denominator] of the exact greatest mean gain over any
    nonempty directed cycle in a strongly connected region.

    The region is a dict with a ``stations`` list and a ``transitions`` list of
    {from, to, gain} edges.  Parallel edges are independent and single-edge
    loops are cycles.  The result is an exact integer fraction with a positive
    denominator.
    """
    stations = region["stations"]
    transitions = region["transitions"]

    index = {s: i for i, s in enumerate(stations)}
    n = len(stations)

    edges = []
    for t in transitions:
        u = index[t["from"]]
        v = index[t["to"]]
        w = t["gain"]
        edges.append((u, v, w))

    # Karp's maximum cycle mean algorithm.  dp[k][v] is the maximum gain of a
    # walk of exactly k edges from node 0 to v.  Because the region is strongly
    # connected, node 0 reaches every node and every cycle is reachable.
    NEG = None
    dp = [[NEG] * n for _ in range(n + 1)]
    dp[0][0] = 0

    for k in range(1, n + 1):
        for u, v, w in edges:
            if dp[k - 1][u] is not None:
                cand = dp[k - 1][u] + w
                if dp[k][v] is None or cand > dp[k][v]:
                    dp[k][v] = cand

    # Karp's theorem: the maximum cycle mean is
    #   max_v min_{0<=k<n} (dp[n][v] - dp[k][v]) / (n - k)
    best = None
    for v in range(n):
        if dp[n][v] is None:
            continue
        vmin = None
        for k in range(n):
            if dp[k][v] is None:
                continue
            num = dp[n][v] - dp[k][v]
            den = n - k
            frac = Fraction(num, den)
            if vmin is None or frac < vmin:
                vmin = frac
        if vmin is not None and (best is None or vmin > best):
            best = vmin

    if best is None:
        return [0, 1]

    return [best.numerator, best.denominator]
"}

The evaluator calls `transform(payload, contract)` in `packages/analysis/engine.py`. The input object described in the business specification is `payload["request"]`. Return the complete JSON-compatible report and leave caller inputs intact. Implement the work in any modules you choose. The included loader, clean-root builder and root delivery command work once the transform is implemented. You can edit the engine, add helpers, and edit run_all.py; retain all other supplied files. Run `python check.py` for the public example.

Independent builds must load the supplied root's input and write outputs/analysis.json. The root command must additionally produce outputs/final_report.json with task "F20", result, and results.analysis. The scorer compares parsed JSON. Object-key order and file whitespace are immaterial. All input cases follow the domain described in the specification.

## Implementation surfaces

The two new helper stubs below may be edited. Implement them and use them within the published transform. The original task, inputs, result schema, and acceptance rules above apply to the complete solution. The helper signatures define source-level interfaces and their local checks can use small in-memory fixtures.

- `packages/analysis/cycle_regions.py` provides `reachable_cycle_regions(request)`. Accept the public request and return a dict with regions and reachable. regions is a list of strongly connected vertex groups that contain at least one directed cycle. Each group is a dict with a stations list and a transitions list containing all original edges internal to that group. reachable maps every station ID to a list of indices of the listed groups it can reach. Include one-vertex self-loop groups and preserve parallel transition rows.
  Local check idea. Use P, A, B, C, and D, with P reaching A and C through A or directly, A and B mutually reachable, C having only a self-loop, and D isolated. Assert that regions have exactly the member sets {'A', 'B'} and {'C'}. P and A can reach both regions, C can reach only its own, and D reaches none. Values may use either region index order.
- `packages/analysis/cycle_mean.py` provides `maximum_cycle_mean(region)`. Accept a cycle-containing strongly connected region with stations and internal transitions. Return a two-integer list [numerator, denominator] with positive denominator representing the exact greatest mean gain over any nonempty directed cycle in that region. Preserve negative means, independent parallel edges, and single-edge loops.
  Local check idea. Pass stations A and B and gains -5 on A to B, -2 on a parallel A to B edge, -3 on B to A, and -6 on A to A. Assert the result is the fraction -5/2. The parallel edge and negative feasible result both affect this check.

The public sustainable map reflects the greatest exact mean among the cycles reachable from each station. Use None for a station that reaches no cycle. Finite approach transitions affect reachability only.

    n = len(stations)

    edges = []
    for t in transitions:
        u = index[t["from"]]
        v = index[t["to"]]
        w = t["gain"]
        edges.append((u, v, w))

    # Karp's maximum cycle mean algorithm.  dp[k][v] is the maximum gain of a
    # walk of exactly k edges from node 0 to v.  Because the region is strongly
    # connected, node 0 reaches every node and every cycle is reachable.
    NEG = None
    dp = [[NEG] * n for _ in range(n + 1)]
    dp[0][0] = 0

    for k in range(1, n + 1):
        for u, v, w in edges:
            if dp[k - 1][u] is not None:
                cand = dp[k - 1][u] + w
                if dp[k][v] is None or cand > dp[k][v]:
                    dp[k][v] = cand

    # Karp's theorem: the maximum cycle mean is
    #   max_v min_{0<=k<n} (dp[n][v] - dp[k][v]) / (n - k)
    best = None
    for v in range(n):
        if dp[n][v] is None:
            continue
        vmin = None
        for k in range(n):
            if dp[k][v] is None:
                continue
            num = dp[n][v] - dp[k][v]
            den = n - k
            frac = Fraction(num, den)
            if vmin is None or frac < vmin:
                vmin = frac
        if vmin is not None and (best is None or vmin > best):
            best = vmin

    if best is None:
        return [0, 1]

    return [best.numerator, best.denominator]
"}

# Sustainable Yield

Implement the business report defined in `packages/analysis/SPEC.md` using Python's standard library. The public input and worked output are `inputs/request.json` and `public_expected.json`.

The evaluator calls `transform(payload, contract)` in `packages/analysis/engine.py`. The input object described in the business specification is `payload["request"]`. Return the complete JSON-compatible report and leave caller inputs intact. Implement the work in any modules you choose. The included loader, clean-root builder and root delivery command work once the transform is implemented. You can edit the engine, add helpers, and edit run_all.py; retain all other supplied files. Run `python check.py` for the public example.

Independent builds must load the supplied root's input and write outputs/analysis.json. The root command must additionally produce outputs/final_report.json with task "F20", result, and results.analysis. The scorer compares parsed JSON. Object-key order and file whitespace are immaterial. All input cases follow the domain described in the specification.

## Implementation surfaces

The two new helper stubs below may be edited. Implement them and use them within the published transform. The original task, inputs, result schema, and acceptance rules above apply to the complete solution. The helper signatures define source-level interfaces and their local checks can use small in-memory fixtures.

- `packages/analysis/cycle_regions.py` provides `reachable_cycle_regions(request)`. Accept the public request and return a dict with regions and reachable. regions is a list of strongly connected vertex groups that contain at least one directed cycle. Each group is a dict with a stations list and a transitions list containing all original edges internal to that group. reachable maps every station ID to a list of indices of the listed groups it can reach. Include one-vertex self-loop groups and preserve parallel transition rows.
  Local check idea. Use P, A, B, C, and D, with P reaching A and C through A or directly, A and B mutually reachable, C having only a self-loop, and D isolated. Assert that regions have exactly the member sets {'A', 'B'} and {'C'}. P and A can reach both regions, C can reach only its own, and D reaches none. Values may use either region index order.
- `packages/analysis/cycle_mean.py` provides `maximum_cycle_mean(region)`. Accept a cycle-containing strongly connected region with stations and internal transitions. Return a two-integer list [numerator, denominator] with positive denominator representing the exact greatest mean gain over any nonempty directed cycle in that region. Preserve negative means, independent parallel edges, and single-edge loops.
  Local check idea. Pass stations A and B and gains -5 on A to B, -2 on a parallel A to B edge, -3 on B to A, and -6 on A to A. Assert the result is the fraction -5/2. The parallel edge and negative feasible result both affect this check.

The public sustainable map reflects the greatest exact mean among the cycles reachable from each station. Use None for a station that reaches no cycle. Finite approach transitions affect reachability only.

from packages.analysis.cycle_regions import reachable_cycle_regions
from packages.analysis.cycle_mean import maximum_cycle_mean


def transform(payload, contract):
    """Return the business report described in SPEC.md. Leave caller inputs unchanged."""
    request = payload["request"]
    data = reachable_cycle_regions(request)
    regions = data["regions"]
    reachable = data["reachable"]

    means = [maximum_cycle_mean(region) for region in regions]

    sustainable = {}
    for station in request["stations"]:
        idxs = reachable.get(station, [])
        if not idxs:
            sustainable[station] = None
            continue
        best = None
        for i in idxs:
            num, den = means[i]
            if best is None or num * best[1] > best[0] * den:
                best = [num, den]
        sustainable[station] = best

    return {"sustainable": sustainable}

    return read(path)

    return build(root, contract, transform)

# Sustainable yield of a production line

stations lists process states. Each directed transition {from,to,gain} consumes exactly one time unit and adds its integer gain; gains may be negative. A controller may choose successive transitions freely. For each start state, find the largest long-run mean gain per time unit it can sustain forever. Equivalently maximize the mean gain of any nonempty directed cycle reachable from this start. A finite approach route affects reachability and contributes nothing to the long-run mean. A state cannot benefit from an unreachable cycle. Loops of one transition are cycles.

Return {sustainable:{station_id:[numerator,denominator] or null}}, with an exact integer fraction of positive denominator, or null if no infinite walk is possible from the station. Equivalent exact fractions are accepted.

"""Generic JSON delivery helpers. Business logic belongs to the submission."""
import json
from pathlib import Path

def read(path):
    return json.loads(Path(path).read_text(encoding="utf-8"))

def save(path, value):
    path = Path(path)
    path.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    path.write_text(json.dumps(value, ensure_ascii=False, allow_nan=False), encoding="utf-8")

def build(root, contract, transform):
    root = Path(root)
    request = read(root / contract["bindings"]["request"])
    result = transform({"request": request}, contract)
    save(root / contract["output"], result)
    return result

# Sustainable yield of a production line

stations lists process states. Each directed transition {from,to,gain} consumes exactly one time unit and adds its integer gain; gains may be negative. A controller may choose successive transitions freely. For each start state, find the largest long-run mean gain per time unit it can sustain forever. Equivalently maximize the mean gain of any nonempty directed cycle reachable from this start. A finite approach route affects reachability and contributes nothing to the long-run mean. A state cannot benefit from an unreachable cycle. Loops of one transition are cycles.

Return {sustainable:{station_id:[numerator,denominator] or null}}, with an exact integer fraction of positive denominator, or null if no infinite walk is possible from the station. Equivalent exact fractions are accepted.

"""Generic JSON delivery helpers. Business logic belongs to the submission."""
import json
from pathlib import Path

def read(path):
    return json.loads(Path(path).read_text(encoding="utf-8"))

def save(path, value):
    path = Path(path)
    path.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    path.write_text(json.dumps(value, ensure_ascii=False, allow_nan=False), encoding="utf-8")

def build(root, contract, transform):
    root = Path(root)
    request = read(root / contract["bindings"]["request"])
    result = transform({"request": request}, contract)
    save(root / contract["output"], result)
    return result

{"packages/analysis/cycle_mean.py": "from fractions import Fraction


def maximum_cycle_mean(region):
    """Return [numerator, denominator] of the exact greatest mean gain over any
    nonempty directed cycle in a strongly connected region.

    The region is a dict with a ``stations`` list and a ``transitions`` list of
    {from, to, gain} edges.  Parallel edges are independent and single-edge
    loops are cycles.  The result is an exact integer fraction with a positive
    denominator.
    """
    stations = region["stations"]
    transitions = region["transitions"]

    index = {s: i for i, s in enumerate(stations)}
    n = len(stations)

    edges = []
    for t in transitions:
        u = index[t["from"]]
        v = index[t["to"]]
        w = t["gain"]
        edges.append((u, v, w))

    # Karp's maximum cycle mean algorithm.  dp[k][v] is the maximum gain of a
    # walk of exactly k edges from node 0 to v.  Because the region is strongly
    # connected, node 0 reaches every node and every cycle is reachable.
    NEG = None
    dp = [[NEG] * n for _ in range(n + 1)]
    dp[0][0] = 0

    for k in range(1, n + 1):
        for u, v, w in edges:
            if dp[k - 1][u] is not None:
                cand = dp[k - 1][u] + w
                if dp[k][v] is None or cand > dp[k][v]:
                    dp[k][v] = cand

    # Karp's theorem: the maximum cycle mean is
    #   max_v min_{0<=k<n} (dp[n][v] - dp[k][v]) / (n - k)
    best = None
    for v in range(n):
        if dp[n][v] is None:
            continue
        vmin = None
        for k in range(n):
            if dp[k][v] is None:
                continue
            num = dp[n][v] - dp[k][v]
            den = n - k
            frac = Fraction(num, den)
            if vmin is None or frac < vmin:
                vmin = frac
        if vmin is not None and (best is None or vmin > best):
            best = vmin

    if best is None:
        return [0, 1]

    return [best.numerator, best.denominator]
"}

# Sustainable Yield

Implement the business report defined in `packages/analysis/SPEC.md` using Python's standard library. The public input and worked output are `inputs/request.json` and `public_expected.json`.

The evaluator calls `transform(payload, contract)` in `packages/analysis/engine.py`. The input object described in the business specification is `payload["request"]`. Return the complete JSON-compatible report and leave caller inputs intact. Implement the work in any modules you choose. The included loader, clean-root builder and root delivery command work once the transform is implemented. You can edit the engine, add helpers, and edit run_all.py; retain all other supplied files. Run `python check.py` for the public example.

Independent builds must load the supplied root's input and write outputs/analysis.json. The root command must additionally produce outputs/final_report.json with task "F20", result, and results.analysis. The scorer compares parsed JSON. Object-key order and file whitespace are immaterial. All input cases follow the domain described in the specification.

## Implementation surfaces

The two new helper stubs below may be edited. Implement them and use them within the published transform. The original task, inputs, result schema, and acceptance rules above apply to the complete solution. The helper signatures define source-level interfaces and their local checks can use small in-memory fixtures.

- `packages/analysis/cycle_regions.py` provides `reachable_cycle_regions(request)`. Accept the public request and return a dict with regions and reachable. regions is a list of strongly connected vertex groups that contain at least one directed cycle. Each group is a dict with a stations list and a transitions list containing all original edges internal to that group. reachable maps every station ID to a list of indices of the listed groups it can reach. Include one-vertex self-loop groups and preserve parallel transition rows.
  Local check idea. Use P, A, B, C, and D, with P reaching A and C through A or directly, A and B mutually reachable, C having only a self-loop, and D isolated. Assert that regions have exactly the member sets {'A', 'B'} and {'C'}. P and A can reach both regions, C can reach only its own, and D reaches none. Values may use either region index order.
- `packages/analysis/cycle_mean.py` provides `maximum_cycle_mean(region)`. Accept a cycle-containing strongly connected region with stations and internal transitions. Return a two-integer list [numerator, denominator] with positive denominator representing the exact greatest mean gain over any nonempty directed cycle in that region. Preserve negative means, independent parallel edges, and single-edge loops.
  Local check idea. Pass stations A and B and gains -5 on A to B, -2 on a parallel A to B edge, -3 on B to A, and -6 on A to A. Assert the result is the fraction -5/2. The parallel edge and negative feasible result both affect this check.

The public sustainable map reflects the greatest exact mean among the cycles reachable from each station. Use None for a station that reaches no cycle. Finite approach transitions affect reachability only.
